program.name: Heterogeneous Learning Systems
program.definition: Study of distribution, organization, use, combination and development of heterogeneous capabilities under constraints.

first_research_dimension.name: Competence heterogeneity
first_research_dimension.qualification: A research priority; increased heterogeneity is not assumed to improve performance and does not redefine HLS.

entities.name: Finite static two-task allocation
entities.definition: Two task types with fixed per-agent effectiveness; demand probability p weights task 1.
entities.scope: Exact, finite, two agents and two task types; scalar effectiveness.
assumptions: No learning or time evolution.

scenario_contract.tasks: Two task types with demand probability p for task 1
scenario_contract.constraints: Compare a common agent across tasks against taskwise access
scenario_contract.uncertainty: No stochastic outcome mechanism required; expected effectiveness is evaluated.

entities.name: Finite effectiveness–resource allocation
entities.definition: Two tasks and agent-specific effectiveness/resource pairs under a fixed resource budget.
entities.scope: Exact finite convexified time-sharing controls.
assumptions: Linear mixing is admissible for the convexified cases.

scenario_contract.capabilities: Fixed effectiveness and resource pair per agent-task
scenario_contract.constraints: Resource budget; time-sharing only where explicitly admissible

entities.name: Two-period competence development
entities.definition: Two agents, two task types and two decision periods; action-dependent change in one competence coordinate.
entities.scope: Deterministic finite analytical testbed.
assumptions: Learning-by-doing transition and terminal routing exactly as specified in THEORY.md.

scenario_contract.tasks: Two task types over two decision periods
scenario_contract.uncertainty: None in the retained exact construction.

entities.name: Synthetic deadline-constrained task queues
entities.definition: Poisson task arrivals, four task families, FCFS single-agent queues, lognormal service and a three-unit deadline.
entities.scope: Synthetic event-driven scenario; three scales and phase-varying demand in the confirmatory study.
assumptions: No learning/cooperation; all conclusions are model-scoped.

scenario_contract.tasks: Four task families arriving in continuous time
scenario_contract.capabilities: Correctness probabilities by agent and task family
scenario_contract.dynamics: Poisson arrivals; service completion and queues
scenario_contract.constraints: FCFS, one service per agent, deadline arrival+3, common admission rule
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Poisson arrivals and lognormal service/correctness outcomes.

entities.name: Stationary task-family queue with fixed competence matrix
entities.definition: Twelve agents and four equiprobable task families under a stationary arrival-mark distribution.
entities.scope: Synthetic paired simulation with N=12, fixed P1 and 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Two specified competence structures only; service/deadline law inherited from the queue model.

scenario_contract.capabilities: Two fixed 12x4 competence matrices with equal per-family means and maxima
scenario_contract.constraints: P1 assignment, FCFS and deadline law inherited from queue scenario

entities.name: Finite sequential problem-belief histories
entities.definition: Sequential FAST/DEEP computations and terminal decision over frozen finite problem-belief domains.
entities.scope: Synthetic confirmatory evaluation across frozen domains/histories.
assumptions: Physical task and observation innovations paired; policy states evolve separately.

scenario_contract.tasks: Finite physical decision problems with sequential computations
scenario_contract.dynamics: Belief/history and computation state evolve by observations
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Frozen finite problem-belief domains and observation innovations.

entities.name: Finite prospective adaptation histories
entities.definition: Finite histories with belief and capability state, policy-dependent decisions and counterfactual continuations.
entities.scope: Synthetic model and frozen reference-state population.
assumptions: Reference-state population is not the full state space.

scenario_contract.tasks: Finite tasks/worlds in a reference-state population
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Finite synthetic worlds; reference population is not full state space.

entities.name: Single-agent task responsibility
entities.definition: One selected agent handles both task types.
entities.scope: Static assignment baseline.
assumptions: Agent identity fixed across task types.

entities.name: Task-wise agent access
entities.definition: A task may be assigned independently to an admissible agent for each type.
entities.scope: Static task routing class.
assumptions: The allowed routing set and any time sharing must be declared.

entities.name: Fixed agent-by-task competence structure
entities.definition: Rows identify agents and columns task families; individual entries remain fixed during evaluation.
entities.scope: General structural representation used by finite and queue models.
assumptions: Entry semantics are model-specific; may be probability or deterministic score.

entities.name: Independent FCFS agent queues
entities.definition: Each agent has one FCFS queue and at most one active task.
entities.scope: Synthetic deadline queue studies.
assumptions: No task cooperation or interruption.

entities.name: Paired generalist and specialist competence matrices
entities.definition: Structure A has three all-high/nine all-low profiles; structure B has three specialists per task family; per-family means/maxima match.
entities.scope: N=12, K=4, values h=.9/l=.6.
assumptions: No claim beyond these two matrices.

entities.name: Static task allocation under heterogeneous effectiveness
entities.definition: Finite model comparing same-agent assignment and task-wise routing for fixed effectiveness.
entities.scope: Two agents/two tasks exact model.
assumptions: Scalar additive expectation over the task mixture.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 fixed effectiveness matrix and task-1 demand probability in [0,1]
entities.inputs: Four assignment expected-effectiveness values, same-agent/taskwise maxima, and their difference

entities.name: Effectiveness–resource frontier allocation
entities.definition: Finite set of assignment points, with a resource budget and upper efficient convex hull.
entities.scope: Two agents/two tasks.
assumptions: Convex hull interpretation requires admissible time-sharing and linear outcome/resource mixtures.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 effectiveness/resource pairs, task demand probability, resource budget
entities.inputs: Feasible policy points, efficient hulls, and best effectiveness under budget
entities.outputs: Finite bicriterion allocation with optional convexified time-sharing.

entities.name: Two-period endogenous competence development
entities.definition: Action-dependent state transition followed by terminal task routing and demand-weighted future value.
entities.scope: Two agents, two tasks, two periods.
assumptions: Deterministic bounded learning-by-doing; no noise, forgetting, or transfer.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 initial competence matrix, action-dependent increments, selected agent, future task mixture
entities.inputs: Post-action competence, terminal assignment outcomes/frontier, immediate/future/total value differences
entities.outputs: Deterministic two-period finite transition and terminal allocation.

entities.name: Dynamic deadline-constrained allocation
entities.definition: Queue state, service times, task correctness, deadline and assignment policy determine on-time collective success.
entities.scope: Synthetic simulator used for confirmatory queue studies.
assumptions: The implementation/results are historical on this branch and not replayable from retained code.
entities.mathematical_object: Task arrivals, queue state, competence matrix or estimates, service-time law, deadlines and policy state
entities.inputs: Agent choice/admission, task completion correctness/timing, collective on-time success and costs
entities.outputs: Discrete-event queue model with one FCFS queue per agent.

entities.name: Sequential computation allocation under belief state
entities.definition: Policy chooses whether to spend additional computation before a terminal decision.
entities.scope: Frozen finite sequential problem-belief design.
assumptions: Different policies induce different histories; randomized baseline did not exactly match realized call counts.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite problem belief/history, computation options, signals, compute cost and stopping choices
entities.inputs: Computation selection, terminal answer, physical reward and compute use
entities.outputs: Sequential decision model; not worker competence allocation.

entities.name: Prospective information and development decision model
entities.definition: Finite belief/capability histories compare myopic and prospective choices with counterfactual continuation.
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic state/reference population.
assumptions: Counterfactual value is model-derived, not an external causal variable.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite state/belief, available information, action-dependent state changes and continuation conditions
entities.inputs: Action choice, counterfactual branch outcomes and model-specific current/future value
entities.outputs: Finite policy and counterfactual models; study-specific state populations.

entities.name: Exact finite model evaluation
entities.definition: Enumerate feasible actions/outcomes and compare exact values/frontiers.
entities.scope: Finite deterministic models.
assumptions: No sampling uncertainty unless stochasticity is explicitly integrated.

entities.name: Paired-replica evaluation
entities.definition: Differences are computed at the independent seed/replica level; bootstrap resamples whole paired replicas.
entities.scope: Simulation campaigns with coupled exogenous/potential outcomes.
assumptions: Tasks inside a replica are not independent replications.

entities.name: Correct completion within deadline rate
entities.definition: Number of tasks both correct and completed by their deadline divided by all arrivals.
entities.scope: Queue/deadline studies.
assumptions: Rejected, wrong, and late tasks count as failures.

entities.name: Static allocation under task-dependent competence
entities.definition: When does task-specific access to fixed competence improve attainable performance?
entities.scope: Finite exact static setting.
assumptions: No learning or dynamics.

entities.name: Crossed specialization exact control
entities.definition: Symmetric two-agent/two-task crossed effectiveness at equal demand.
entities.scope: p=.5; effectiveness entries 1.0 and .2.

entities.name: Exact gain from task-wise allocation in crossed specialization
entities.definition: Task-wise routing obtains effectiveness 1.0 versus .6 for the best one-agent policy; difference .4.
entities.scope: Exact two-agent/two-task instance at p=.5.
assumptions: Fixed effectiveness; scalar additive expected effectiveness.

entities.name: Dynamic competence change and future value
entities.definition: Can action-induced competence change affect the collective frontier, future value, and current choice?
entities.scope: Exact deterministic two-period testbed.
assumptions: No empirical calibration.

entities.name: Learning-induced state change with unchanged efficient frontier
entities.definition: Compare two action-induced terminal states under identical future demand.
entities.scope: Initial state ((.4,.8),(.8,.4)); learning rate (.1,0).

entities.name: Future-value reversal control
entities.definition: Compare current and future value differences in a finite two-period decision.
entities.scope: Initial state ((.7,.8),(.8,.6)); learning rate (.3,0); future task-1 probability .75.

entities.name: State change need not alter efficient collective capability
entities.definition: The two resulting states differ but both frontiers equal {(0.8,0.8)} and future-value difference is zero.
entities.scope: Exact finite construction.

entities.name: Future development value can reverse an immediate preference
entities.definition: At p=.75, immediate difference is -.1, future development value is +.15, and total difference is +.05.
entities.scope: Exact finite construction.

entities.name: Joint and separated policy-class boundary
entities.definition: Under what exact finite assumptions does joint operation/development outperform a restricted separated class?
entities.scope: Common-world finite policy comparison.
assumptions: Common information, actions, rewards, resources and physics; finite attained optima for iff result.

entities.name: Separated policy-class inclusion
entities.definition: A separated class constrained to greedy routing is a subset of the unrestricted joint class; maximizing over a superset cannot lower value.
entities.scope: Common-world/common-information contract.
assumptions: Same feasible world and objective.

entities.name: Sequential computation selection under performance-cost trade-offs
entities.definition: Does prospective computation selection improve cumulative task reward and computation cost in a frozen finite design?
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic problem-belief histories/domains.
assumptions: No exactly matched realized invocation rate; timings machine-sensitive.

entities.name: Scoped sequential computation trade-off
entities.definition: A prospective computation selector versus a nominally equal-rate randomized rule: +.1167 cumulative physical reward/history [0.0310,0.2013] and −.1924 seconds/history [−.3539,−.0228].
entities.scope: Confirmatory paired histories in the frozen design.
assumptions: Intervals are paired history-level intervals as reported.

entities.name: Joint error dependence and collective majority risk
entities.definition: Can joint error dependence change majority risk when individual error marginals are fixed?
entities.scope: Exact three-classifier probability laws.
assumptions: No classifier model inference.

entities.name: Same error marginal, different majority risk
entities.definition: Both joint laws give individual error .20; majority risk is .30 under law A and .20 under law B.
entities.scope: Exact synthetic joint distributions.

entities.name: Transfer and fixed-organization collective performance
entities.definition: Does transfer improve an individual while reducing collective performance, and does reorganization recover it?
entities.scope: Three synthetic binary tasks; 20 paired seeds in second iteration.
assumptions: V1 had target-label leakage; V2 intervals include zero.

entities.name: Transfer advantage and collective effect not established
entities.scope: Twenty paired synthetic seeds.

entities.name: Competence structure, assignment policy and scale in deadline queues
entities.definition: How do mean-preserving competence profiles, allocation policy and scale relate to on-time collective task success?
entities.scope: Synthetic dynamic queue, N=12/24/48, four task families, 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: One synthetic queue/service/deadline model; no learning/cooperation; P1 not globally optimal.

entities.name: Factorial deadline-queue comparison
entities.definition: Three competence compositions × four policies × three scales, 30 seeds; 1080 valid replicas.
entities.scope: Poisson arrivals; lognormal service; FCFS; deadline +3.

entities.name: Mean-preserving profile contrast under information-complete assignment
entities.scope: Thirty paired seeds per scale; synthetic model.

entities.name: Estimated competence lagged the information-complete reference
entities.scope: Thirty paired seeds per scale; synthetic model.

entities.name: External competence calibration and load filtering
entities.definition: How do external calibration and an admissibility load filter affect P2?
entities.scope: Synthetic queue, H2, N=12 and N=48.
assumptions: Results only for one model and selected scales.

entities.name: External calibration improved on-time success in the tested P2 setting
entities.scope: Paired synthetic replicas.

entities.name: Descriptive diagnostics of composition effects
entities.definition: Reanalysis of selection, load and waiting metrics for the deadline-queue factorial.
entities.scope: Reuses 90 existing N=24/P1 replicas.
assumptions: Not an independent replication and no causal mediation identification.

entities.name: Joint competence structure under matched marginals
entities.definition: Do two distinct joint competence matrices with the same per-task mean and maximum differ under fixed allocation?
entities.scope: Stationary synthetic queue; N=12, K=4; 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Two matrices only; one policy/demand law; no causal mediator established.

entities.name: Paired comparison of two matched-marginal competence structures
entities.definition: Two structures evaluated under the same seed-specific demand and potential outcomes; 60 valid simulation runs.
entities.scope: 30 seed pairs; one N and fixed policy.

entities.name: Different joint structures yielded different performance at equal marginals
entities.definition: B−A success-on-time +21.52 pp, SD 1.13, paired bootstrap 95% interval [21.12,21.92], positive in 30/30 pairs.
entities.scope: Synthetic N=12 queue; 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Structures have per-family mean .675 and max .9.

entities.name: Assignment sensitivity and future opportunity
entities.definition: Finite analyses of assignment, learning opportunity, and continuation value.
entities.scope: Constructed finite decision processes.
assumptions: No empirical or general-planner validation.

entities.name: Prospective information and development anticipation
entities.definition: Finite adaptation studies compare prospective information/development decisions and realized return.
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic policy and state populations.
assumptions: Conditional reference state bank; exact experiment-specific semantics.

entities.name: Static feasible outcome set
entities.definition: For fixed state, demand, constraints, and admissible policy class, the feasible outcome set is the outcomes induced by feasible policies.
entities.scope: Definition; static model scope.
assumptions: Outcome map and feasibility set must be specified.

entities.name: Crossed-specialization gain formula
entities.definition: Under strict crossed advantage, routing gain is min(p A1,(1-p) A2), with maximum A1 A2/(A1+A2).
entities.scope: Two agents, two tasks, scalar additive effectiveness.
assumptions: Fixed competence and equal-resource model; p is task-1 probability.

entities.name: Competence-state change need not change efficient frontier
entities.definition: Different action-induced states may have identical efficient collective outcome frontiers.
entities.scope: Exact finite counterexample.
assumptions: The frontier is computed from the same terminal routing set.

entities.name: Future capability value depends on future conditions
entities.definition: Different future capabilities can have equal value; a future value difference can reverse an immediate ranking.
entities.scope: Two-period finite construction.
assumptions: Future demand and objective are declared; values are model-specific.

entities.name: Current and continuation value decomposition
entities.definition: In the stated two-period decision, total difference equals current difference plus future development-value difference.
entities.scope: Two-period finite construction and standard continuation value.
assumptions: Common objective and exact transition/value calculation.

entities.name: Joint policy-class value inclusion
entities.definition: Under a common world/information contract, a separated policy class constrained to a subset of actions is contained in the joint class; its maximum value cannot be larger.
entities.scope: Finite common-world decision model.
assumptions: Same feasible world, observations, rewards, resources, objective.

entities.name: Joint error law affects majority risk at fixed individual marginals
entities.definition: Two specified joint laws with marginal error .20 yield majority risks .30 and .20.
entities.scope: Exact three-classifier probability construction.
assumptions: These are the supplied joint laws; not a general theorem about time or AI aging.

entities.name: Finite opportunity-sensitive decisions
entities.definition: Finite state and action constructions in which present assignment can change future opportunity/value.
entities.scope: Synthetic finite decision process.
assumptions: Model-specific transition, information, and continuation-value assumptions.

scenario_contract.dynamics: Finite state transitions and continuation values
scenario_contract.constraints: Model-specific action, information and resource feasibility

entities.name: Assignment sensitivity and continuation value
entities.definition: A finite Bellman analysis connecting an assignment choice to opportunity-dependent continuation value.
entities.scope: Constructed finite states and actions.
assumptions: Local ranking inversion alone does not establish a root-level value gap.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite assignment state/action alternatives, transition and continuation values
entities.inputs: Local ranking and root-level policy value comparisons
entities.outputs: Finite Bellman analysis; local inversion alone is insufficient.

entities.name: Persistence interaction boundary analysis
entities.definition: A planned factorial asked whether architecture, demand persistence and learning interact; a separate fixed-competence fixture evaluated a restricted estimand.
entities.scope: The planned campaign was not run; the retained analytical fixtures are narrower.
assumptions: The fixed-competence fixture does not estimate the unexecuted learning interaction.

entities.name: Competence-improvement priority statistic checks
entities.definition: Exact checks examine whether failure frequency multiplied by quality gap is sufficient to rank improvement opportunities.
entities.scope: Model-specific thresholds, null cases and ranking reversals.
assumptions: No universal priority rule is established.

entities.name: Bounded reproductions of published organization mechanisms
entities.definition: Selected published mechanisms were represented in bounded executable checks to assess correspondence and reuse.
entities.scope: Mechanism-specific bounded reproductions; distinct source mechanisms remain separate.
assumptions: Passing a bounded check is not evidence of general HLS performance.

entities.name: Portfolio learning and interference pilots
entities.definition: Pilot studies examined portfolio learning, opportunity, interference and compatibility in distinct bounded settings.
entities.scope: Multiple protocols and task/data settings; pooled results are not a common estimand.
assumptions: Some cross-protocol comparisons failed compatibility; no general training policy is established.

entities.name: Contextual model selection under quality and latency
entities.definition: A small held-out comparison evaluated dynamic selection among fixed model candidates under quality and latency measurements.
entities.scope: 160 held-out queries; corrected timing and provenance issues are documented.
assumptions: A retrospective oracle is not deployable; small sample and timing limits apply.

entities.name: Model routing under an inference budget
entities.definition: A predictor and a budgeted optimizer were evaluated separately against declared baselines.
entities.scope: Specific predictor/optimizer pilot cells.
assumptions: Predictor and optimizer effects are distinct; one cell does not establish general superiority.

entities.name: Classifier fusion under joint error dependence
entities.definition: Synthetic exact calculations examined coalition accuracy under specified dependence mixtures.
entities.scope: Constructed joint error laws and three-classifier majority examples.
assumptions: No real model inference or general fusion result.

entities.name: Model-specific execution and evaluation contracts
entities.definition: Engineering checks tested bounded provenance-carrying execution/evaluation interfaces across selected model implementations.
entities.scope: Technical vertical slices and contract tests only.
assumptions: Common serialization does not imply mathematical equivalence.

entities.name: Production, competence learning and teaching integration
entities.definition: Bounded model integrations examined production and learning/teaching components with distinct competence and productivity semantics.
entities.scope: Tracked records are incomplete; a larger local artifact was not published and a later campaign was interrupted.
assumptions: Nembhard productivity is not interchangeable with competence; broad outcome is not verifiable.

entities.name: Empirical data vehicle feasibility screening
entities.definition: Feasibility gates assessed whether candidate datasets could support required structural and competence measurements.
entities.scope: Screening only; no empirical validation.
assumptions: No real-world performance claim.

entities.name: State and trajectory discrimination checks
entities.definition: Exploratory gates evaluated whether generated state/trajectory populations had support and discrimination for later comparisons.
entities.scope: Technical diagnostics; not confirmatory policy evaluation.
assumptions: No policy value estimand established.

entities.name: Counterfactual label and engine equivalence gate
entities.definition: A technical gate tested whether counterfactual labels and engine outputs supported a proposed larger comparison; the gate failed.
entities.scope: The planned larger campaign did not execute.
assumptions: A negative gate is not a scientific policy-effect result.

entities.name: Restricted persistence-interaction fixtures
entities.definition: The registered 960-run question was not executed; the fixed-competence stationary equal-marginal fixture has zero expected persistence interaction, while a separate finite fixture reports Θ(1)=−.003.
entities.scope: Analytical fixtures only.

entities.name: Priority statistic lacks universal sufficiency
entities.definition: Exact checks include nulls, thresholds and ranking reversals; they do not validate failure-frequency times quality-gap as a universal selector.
entities.scope: Model-specific exact checks.

entities.name: Bounded mechanism correspondence checks
entities.definition: Selected published mechanisms received bounded executable checks; these do not establish end-to-end HLS performance or general reproduction fidelity.
entities.scope: Technical validation only.

entities.name: Portfolio compatibility and interference findings
entities.definition: Cross-model bridges include failed compatibility, inconclusive portfolio cases and bounded interference/replay findings; protocols do not share one estimand.
entities.scope: Multiple bounded pilots, reported separately in source records.

entities.name: Small held-out model-selection comparison
entities.definition: Corrected comparison reports quality 46.25 versus 45.0 and latency 139.27 versus 141.61 ms; quality difference +1.25 with interval [−1.25,3.75].
entities.scope: 160 held-out queries; timing/provenance corrections apply.

entities.name: Budgeted routing predictor and optimizer results
entities.definition: One predictor scored Brier .2698 versus constant .2314 and logistic .2174; a clear optimizer gain of +2.16 pp was reported in one cell.
entities.scope: Specific pilot configurations only.

entities.name: Synthetic classifier-fusion dependence calculations
entities.definition: Exact mixture check reports coalition accuracy .826 at correlation parameter 0, .700 at 1 and .7945 at .25; separate majority-law result is registered independently.
entities.scope: Constructed synthetic laws; not real inference.

entities.name: Bounded execution-contract validation
entities.definition: Selected technical vertical slices and tests passed without establishing a universal execution abstraction or model equivalence.
entities.scope: Technical validation only.

entities.name: Production-learning integration evidence incomplete
entities.definition: Twenty-nine tracked records were available; a reported 1,016-run local artifact was unpublished and a later campaign was interrupted.
entities.scope: No completed independently verifiable campaign.

entities.name: Empirical vehicle feasibility screen only
entities.definition: The screening stopped at feasibility gates and produced no empirical outcome validation.
entities.scope: Candidate data feasibility only.

entities.name: State and trajectory support diagnostics
entities.definition: Finite gate diagnostics recorded support/discrimination limits; no confirmatory policy-value estimate was produced.
entities.scope: Technical gate only.

entities.name: Counterfactual engine equivalence gate failed
entities.definition: Control labels were not equivalent, so the proposed larger run received NO-GO and did not execute.
entities.scope: Technical negative; no policy-effect estimate.

entities.name: Contextual selection under changing rewards and selective feedback
entities.definition: Studies contextual action selection under nonstationary outcomes, selective observations, memory and assignment.
entities.scope: Distinct simulation factors and estimands; source campaign records are not combined into one effect.
assumptions: Reported algorithm variants are not all faithful implementations of named standard procedures.
Observation can be endogenous to assignment.

entities.name: Selective-feedback contextual selection effects are cell-specific
entities.definition: In one shared-feedback infrequent-change cell, a windowed method had regret 184.88 versus 259.47 (difference −74.59, interval [−89.60,−59.58]); closed-loop intervals included zero.
entities.scope: Exploratory cell-specific comparisons; not pooled across distinct estimands.
assumptions: The source record reports candidate algorithms that differ in more than memory.

entities.name: Static constrained assignment comparison
entities.definition: Exact finite comparison of task assignment choices under a static effectiveness objective.
entities.scope: Constructed finite allocation case; no temporal state transition.
assumptions: Constructed finite objective, action set and resource semantics as stated by the historical source.

entities.name: Static constrained assignment comparison reported exact values
entities.definition: Reported S1 value comparison: 2.6 versus 1.8.
entities.scope: Historical finite constructions; detailed execution artifacts are not retained on this branch.
assumptions: Values are scoped to their individual constructed cases.

entities.name: Shared-budget temporal optimization
entities.definition: Finite dynamic decisions with shared resource budgets and continuation value.
entities.scope: S2 cases are distinct constructions; Bellman and myopic values are not pooled into one estimator.
assumptions: Constructed finite objective, action set and resource semantics as stated by the historical source.

entities.name: Shared-budget temporal optimization reported exact values
entities.definition: Reported S2a exact 8 versus greedy 7.2; S2b Bellman 1 versus myopic .9 with sufficient budget 1.9.
entities.scope: Historical finite constructions; detailed execution artifacts are not retained on this branch.
assumptions: Values are scoped to their individual constructed cases.

entities.name: Load-only feasible queue dispatch
entities.definition: Selects an admissible agent using expected pending workload; ignores competence.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No competence information is used.
entities.inputs: Queue state, eligibility and estimated workload

entities.name: Known-competence deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Ranks admissible agents by true task competence multiplied by estimated probability of on-time completion.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: True competence is available only to the information-complete reference.
entities.inputs: Task type, true competence and observable workload/service/deadline state

entities.name: Estimated-competence deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Uses the same competence-times-deadline score as the information-complete rule, substituting Beta-Bernoulli estimates updated on observed outcomes.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No hidden competence or future outcome is observed.
entities.inputs: Task type, prior observed task outcomes, and observable operational state

entities.name: Contextual deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Adapts dispatch choices using a disjoint linear upper-confidence policy with context equal to deadline feasibility times task-family indicator.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Feedback is updated only when its specified reward becomes observable.
entities.inputs: Observable context, delayed binary on-time-correct reward and feasibility state

entities.name: Same-agent multi-task assignment
entities.definition: Requires one agent identity to handle all task types in the static comparison.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No learning or time evolution.
entities.inputs: Fixed effectiveness matrix and task demand
entities.outputs: Selected common agent and expected effectiveness

entities.name: Taskwise competence assignment
entities.definition: Allows the selected agent to vary by task type under the declared feasible access class.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Feasible assignment/access class is declared; any convexification is separate.
entities.inputs: Fixed effectiveness matrix and task demand
entities.outputs: Task-specific agent choices and expected effectiveness

entities.name: Prospective computation selector
entities.definition: Selects additional computation from available prospective signals in a finite sequential problem-belief setting.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Observed call rates differ from nominal target in the confirmatory comparison.
entities.inputs: Belief/history features and computation costs
entities.outputs: Continue/stop or computation choice and terminal decision

entities.name: Synthetic joint classifier error laws
entities.definition: Finite joint Bernoulli error distributions with specified marginals and dependence.
entities.scope: Three classifier variables; exact probability law; majority decision.
assumptions: Constructed laws; no inference on real models.

scenario_contract.tasks: One common classification instance abstracted to correctness/error
scenario_contract.capabilities: Marginal error probability .20 for each classifier in the specified laws

entities.name: Synthetic transfer and classification tasks
entities.definition: Three generated binary classification tasks with separate train/validation/test examples and one donor-to-recipient distillation comparison.
entities.scope: Task distributions and the train/test overlap defect in the first iteration are methodologically relevant.
assumptions: V2 contrasts remain inconclusive; raw predictions are not retained.

scenario_contract.agents: Donor classifier A3 and recipient classifier A1, with other baseline models
scenario_contract.capabilities: Task-specific classifier performance and donor output probabilities
scenario_contract.dynamics: Initial training, then one recipient update on task 3
scenario_contract.constraints: Paired seeds; held-out test; no hyperparameter change after test
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Synthetic data generation and model initialization.

entities.name: Fixed candidate-model query evaluation
entities.definition: Held-out query set evaluated by a fixed set of model candidates with answer-quality and latency outputs.
entities.scope: Corrected held-out subset of 160 queries.
assumptions: Timing is machine-sensitive; retrospective oracle is not deployable.

scenario_contract.dynamics: Static candidates; contextual selection per query
scenario_contract.constraints: Held-out query evaluation; no deployable retrospective oracle

entities.name: Budgeted model-query routing
entities.definition: Model candidate routing evaluated under a compute or latency budget with predictor and optimizer components.
entities.scope: Pilot cells and declared routing budgets.
assumptions: Predictor quality and optimizer utility are distinct estimands.

scenario_contract.tasks: Queries with output-quality and compute/latency budget
scenario_contract.capabilities: Predicted candidate outcome and measured costs
scenario_contract.constraints: Declared pilot budget and candidate set

entities.name: Joint error and majority-risk model
entities.definition: Maps a joint distribution over classifier error indicators to marginal and collective majority risk.
entities.scope: Finite binary error vector and deterministic majority aggregation.
assumptions: Pairwise covariance does not determine a general higher-order joint law.
entities.inputs: Marginal errors, pair dependence and collective majority risk
entities.mathematical_object: Joint distribution over binary classifier error indicators and a decision aggregation rule

entities.name: Recipient update by supervised learning and distillation
entities.definition: Compares a recipient classifier after label-based refit, aligned donor distillation, and permuted-output control.
entities.scope: Synthetic binary classification tasks; paired seeds.
assumptions: Comparison C2-C1 changes information target as well as transfer; estimates do not establish a pure transfer effect.
entities.inputs: Recipient performance under supervised, aligned-distillation and permuted-output controls
entities.mathematical_object: Synthetic task examples, labels, donor probability outputs and recipient model update conditions

entities.name: Fixed candidate quality-latency comparison
entities.definition: Evaluates predicted/contextual choice among fixed candidate models using quality and latency outputs.
entities.scope: Corrected held-out query records.
assumptions: Small held-out set; timing and code-provenance incidents are documented.
entities.inputs: Candidate selection, answer-quality score and latency
entities.mathematical_object: Held-out queries, fixed candidate outputs, quality labels/metrics and measured latency

entities.name: Finite service and assignment solver checks
entities.definition: Bounded finite solver checks compare assignment values/frontiers under model-specific service assumptions and tie rules.
entities.scope: Distinct finite formulations are retained as a family record only; their values are not pooled.
assumptions: Service, tie-breaking and feasible planner classes are model-specific.
entities.research_question: How do service assumptions, assignment rules and tie handling affect finite solver comparisons?

entities.name: Finite solver values depend on service and tie semantics
entities.definition: Historical records report finite values/frontiers and tie-rule sensitivity; these are distinct model-specific checks, not a pooled effect.
entities.scope: Bounded exact solver cases.
assumptions: No common cross-case estimand is asserted.

entities.name: SOC alert triage and deep analysis testbed
entities.definition: A proposed simplified application scenario for studying how heterogeneous human cyberanalyst competences are characterized, used and potentially developed across initial alert triage (L1) and deeper alert analysis (L2). It is a research specification, not a verified description of a particular client SOC.
entities.scope: Multi-client security operations are in scope as an application context; new clients, technologies and threats are possible future conditions. No operational dataset or client-specific process has been verified.
assumptions: L1 and L2 are distinct conceptual processes supplied for this testbed; their workflow, authority, handoff and decision order in any real SOC remain unverified.
Analysts may differ in experience, knowledge and competence, but no individual competence values, distributions or validated measurement instruments are supplied.
Experience is not treated as a competence measurement or as evidence of learning.
Learning by doing, deliberate development, knowledge transfer, specialization and adaptation are candidate mechanisms, not established properties or guaranteed benefits.
Workload, alert classes, client mix, service times, deadlines, outcomes, costs, access rights and resource constraints require application-specific evidence or explicit future assumptions.

scenario_contract.agents: Human cyberanalysts; heterogeneity in experience, knowledge and task-conditioned competence is part of the proposed scenario, but no individual data or distributions are available.
scenario_contract.tasks: L1 initial alert triage with two decisions (escalate or not; report or not); L2 deeper investigation of alerts designated for deeper analysis. Decision ordering and task taxonomy are unspecified.
scenario_contract.capabilities: Individual competence and capability must be operationalized separately; no competence values or measurement model are supplied. Collective attainable capability and realized collective performance are distinct targets.
scenario_contract.dynamics: The application may include multiple/new clients, technologies and threats. Arrival, client-mix, threat, learning, development, transfer and adaptation dynamics are unspecified.
scenario_contract.constraints: Real SOC staffing, authority, client contracts, tools, privacy/security rules, queue discipline, deadlines/SLA, resource limits and escalation/reporting procedures are not verified; they must be specified before modeling.
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Alert truth/outcomes, competence, workload, service duration, client context and threat novelty may be uncertain or partially observed; distributions and observation processes are not supplied.

processes.name: Initial alert triage
processes.description: For an alert entering initial triage, represent the supplied decisions “escalate or not” and “report or not”. The relation and timing between the decisions must be specified for each future study; this is not asserted as the client’s real procedure.

processes.name: Deep alert analysis
processes.description: Represent investigation of alerts requiring deeper analysis. Entry criteria, outputs, staffing and handoff from L1 are unresolved modeling choices, not verified client facts.

entities.provenance_status: Scenario scope comes from the 2026-10-27 research instruction. Historical repository audit material did not verify SOCTRA fields or client-level operational data; no AIAI 2026 organizational-learning result is available as evidence for this scenario.

entities.name: Competence heterogeneity in SOC alert operations: proposed testbed
entities.definition: A proposed application testbed to investigate characterization and use of heterogeneous competencies in initial alert triage and deeper alert analysis, with possible later questions about development, adaptation, costs and limitations.
entities.scope: Proposal only. No model, protocol, data, experiment, result or real-SOC validation has been approved or executed.
assumptions: The scenario contract and operational facts must be established before a study model or experiment is specified.
entities.research_question: How should competence heterogeneity among cyberanalysts be characterized, and under what evidenced workload, organizational and resource conditions does its utilization or development affect individual and collective performance across L1 triage and L2 analysis?
entities.first_research_dimension: Competence heterogeneity: characterization, utilization, development, adaptation, benefits, costs and limitations; no direction of effect is presumed.
planned_mechanisms: adaptation to clients, technologies and threats
entities.mechanism_status: Candidates for future, separately specified research; none is claimed to describe actual client procedures or to improve performance.

entities.name: Finite deterministic sequence of typed tasks
entities.definition: An ordered finite sequence of typed tasks evaluated under fixed deterministic agent-by-task effectiveness.
entities.scope: Small exact benchmark instances; no stochastic arrivals or outcome draws.
assumptions: Task types and their order are fixed inputs.
Every agent is eligible for every task type; capacity is the only assignment feasibility constraint.
The evaluation horizon is the number of received tasks.

scenario_contract.tasks: A non-empty ordered sequence of K task-type indices.
scenario_contract.capabilities: A separate deterministic effectiveness matrix e[i,k] with entries in [0,1]; not a competence observation.
scenario_contract.dynamics: Task index advances after each decision; effectiveness is fixed.
scenario_contract.constraints: Each assignment consumes one unit from the selected agent's non-negative integer capacity; rejection consumes none.
scenario_contract.uncertainty: None in task order, effectiveness contribution, or state transition.

entities.name: Agents with finite integer task capacities
entities.definition: An indexed agent set with fixed initial integer capacities and complete eligibility across the declared task types.
entities.scope: Finite deterministic allocation benchmark.
assumptions: One task consumes exactly one capacity unit.
Capacities do not replenish during the sequence.

entities.name: Sequential deterministic allocation under finite capacity
entities.definition: At each task position, assign the current task to one eligible agent or reject it; assignments consume integer capacity and contribute fixed e[i,k] to a total objective.
entities.scope: Finite ordered tasks, fixed effectiveness matrix, no queues, deadlines, learning, cooperation, or uncertainty.
assumptions: Effectiveness is a deterministic contribution in [0,1], not a latent competence value or observed success.
Rejected tasks contribute zero; mean performance divides by all tasks received.
The offline policy enumerates feasible choices and is intended only for small instances.
entities.mathematical_object: Ordered task-type sequence, fixed N-by-K effectiveness matrix, remaining integer capacities, and a feasible assignment-or-rejection action at each position.
entities.inputs: Task types, deterministic effectiveness values, initial capacities, and (for the fixed policy) a predeclared type-to-agent mapping.
entities.outputs: Per-task decisions/rejection causes, remaining capacity, total effectiveness, and mean over all received tasks.

entities.name: Fixed task-type-to-agent assignment
entities.definition: Uses a mapping declared before the sequence; does not reassign when its designated agent is exhausted.
entities.scope: Sequential finite-capacity benchmark.
assumptions: If the designated agent is exhausted while another agent has capacity, rejection is policy-induced; global saturation is recorded separately.
entities.inputs: Current task type, remaining capacity of the designated agent, and the fixed mapping.
entities.outputs: Assign to the mapped agent or reject.

entities.name: Greedy online assignment by current effectiveness
entities.definition: Assigns the current task to the feasible agent with greatest e[i,k], breaking ties by ascending agent index.
entities.scope: Sequential finite-capacity benchmark; online information only.
assumptions: The decision rule observes only the current task type and remaining capacities; it cannot inspect future tasks.
entities.inputs: Current task type, remaining capacities, and fixed effectiveness matrix.
entities.outputs: A feasible agent assignment or global-capacity rejection.

entities.name: Exact offline allocation by enumeration
entities.definition: Uses the full task sequence and enumerates assignment-or-rejection sequences to maximize total deterministic effectiveness under capacities.
entities.scope: Small finite benchmark instances; exponential enumeration.
assumptions: This is a hindsight oracle with future information, not an online policy.
Ties keep the lexicographically first sequence with agent indices ascending and rejection last.
Objective sums are compared exactly for the supplied numeric entries; binary floating-point entries are treated as their exact represented values.
entities.inputs: Full task sequence, fixed effectiveness matrix, and initial capacities.

entities.name: Total and mean effectiveness per received task
entities.definition: Reports the sum of assigned-task effectiveness and that sum divided by all tasks received; rejected tasks contribute zero.
entities.scope: Finite deterministic sequential assignment.
assumptions: The denominator includes assigned and rejected tasks.
Rejection causes and assigned-task counts are reported separately.

entities.name: Sequential deterministic task allocation under finite capacity
entities.definition: Consolidate a deterministic benchmark for fixed, greedy online, and exact offline assignment policies under fixed heterogeneous effectiveness and finite agent capacity.
entities.scope: First bounded HLS-01 increment; constructed finite controls only, not an empirical application or CE-04 reproduction.
assumptions: Effectiveness entries are deterministic contributions in [0,1].
No stochastic demand, queues, deadlines, learning, cooperation, or AI intervention.
entities.research_question: How do a predeclared fixed mapping and a greedy online policy compare with exact offline allocation on finite deterministic typed-task sequences under fixed effectiveness and integer agent capacities?

entities.name: Deterministic controls for sequential assignment policies
entities.definition: Runner control suite checks static compatibility, two static nulls, capacity-limited greedy suboptimality, and rejection-cause accounting.
entities.scope: Small hand-specified finite cases; deterministic execution, no sampling inference.
assumptions: Control cases validate implementation behavior only and are not empirical evidence.

entities.name: Sequential benchmark recovers static allocation controls
entities.definition: With non-restrictive capacities, fixed type-to-agent mappings and greedy taskwise selection reproduce StaticAllocationModel policy values for crossed specialization, homogeneous null, and taskwise-dominance null controls.
entities.scope: Deterministic control fixtures defined in the benchmark runner.
assumptions: The sequential objective is mean deterministic effectiveness over the empirical task sequence.
Capacity does not bind in these controls.

entities.name: Greedy online assignment can be suboptimal under finite capacity
entities.definition: In one two-task, two-agent fixture, greedy obtains total effectiveness 1.0 while exact offline enumeration obtains 1.7 under capacities (1,1). This is a constructed counterexample, not a general effect estimate.
entities.scope: Tasks (type 0, type 1); effectiveness rows (1.0,0.8) and (0.9,0.0); capacities (1,1).
assumptions: Effectiveness is deterministic, tasks are ordered, and offline access to the full sequence is allowed.

entities.name: Finite temporal arrivals with recoverable service capacity
entities.definition: A finite ordered stream of typed tasks arriving over a declared horizon; service jobs may remain queued at the horizon and are then drained to completion.
entities.scope: Deterministic one-server-per-agent FCFS allocation controls; arrival times and task types are constructed inputs.
assumptions: Every task arrival is an abstract task instance; an SOCTRA alert record is not assumed to be a human work episode.
All arrival times lie in [0,H), and all queued tasks are processed after the arrival horizon.
Demand, effectiveness and service parameters are held identical across compared policies.

scenario_contract.agents: N agents; each has one service server.
scenario_contract.tasks: Finite ordered pairs (arrival_time, task_type), with K task types.
scenario_contract.capabilities: Fixed deterministic effectiveness e[i,k] in [0,1], distinct from competence or observed success.
scenario_contract.dynamics: One FCFS service queue per agent; service capacity returns when the current task completes.
scenario_contract.constraints: One task in service per agent; queues are unbounded; no task rejection.
scenario_contract.uncertainty: None in arrival sequence, service duration or effectiveness in each control.

entities.name: Agents with one recoverable FCFS service server
entities.definition: Each agent has one non-preemptive server and one unbounded first-come, first-served queue; the next queued task begins at prior completion.
entities.scope: Deterministic temporal allocation model.
assumptions: The queue order follows arrival order; simultaneous arrivals retain input order.
Service capacity is released at completion; no other availability or staffing schedule is modeled.

entities.name: Deterministic temporal FCFS task allocation
entities.definition: At each arrival, an online policy assigns the task to one agent queue. A task starts at the later of its arrival and that agent queue tail, occupies the server for its class-specific deterministic duration, and contributes fixed e[i,k] at completion.
entities.scope: Finite arrivals, fixed effectiveness, deterministic service durations shared by agents within task class, unbounded FCFS queues, all tasks drained to completion.
assumptions: Service times are hypothetical positive scenario parameters, not SOCTRA measurements.
One server per agent; no preemption, rejection, deadlines, learning, cooperation or stochastic success.
Effectiveness is independent of queue position and service duration.
entities.mathematical_object: Arrival stream (t_n,k_n), e[i,k], class durations s_k, per-agent queue-tail completion times and one online assignment action at each arrival.
entities.inputs: Ordered arrivals, fixed effectiveness matrix, positive deterministic service time per task class, arrival horizon, and (for fixed policy) predeclared class-to-agent mapping.
entities.outputs: Assignment trace, service starts/completions, effectiveness contributions, waits, responses, per-agent utilization, horizon backlog and makespan.

entities.name: Fixed temporal assignment by task class
entities.definition: Routes each arrival to a predeclared agent for its task class; the task joins that agent FCFS queue regardless of current workload.
entities.scope: Online; mapping fixed before the sequence is evaluated.
assumptions: No reassignment or future-demand access.
entities.inputs: Current task class and frozen type-to-agent mapping.

entities.name: Temporal assignment by maximum fixed effectiveness
entities.definition: Routes the current task to an agent maximizing e[i,k], with ties broken by ascending agent index; it does not use queue workload.
entities.scope: Online; all tasks eventually complete under unbounded queues.
assumptions: Effectiveness values are fixed and all agents are eligible for all task classes.
entities.inputs: Current task class and fixed effectiveness matrix.

entities.name: Temporal assignment by effectiveness-to-workload ratio
entities.definition: Routes the current task to an agent maximizing e[i,k]/(W_i+s_k), where W_i is its observable remaining active service plus queued service; ties go to the lowest agent index.
entities.scope: Online deterministic heuristic; not claimed optimal.
assumptions: Service durations and queue-tail workload are known at decision time.
No future arrivals, service completions beyond current state, or task outcomes are consulted.
entities.inputs: Current task class, fixed effectiveness matrix, current queue-tail times and current time.

entities.name: Temporal task effectiveness, delay, backlog and utilization
entities.definition: Reports task-level deterministic effectiveness and temporal workload metrics for all M received tasks under an arrival horizon H, followed by queue drain.
entities.scope: Deterministic temporal allocation controls and horizon-completion views.
assumptions: Time uses the scenario service-time unit.
P95 uses empirical nearest rank, sorted value at rank ceil(0.95 M).
Utilization is measured only over [0,H); tasks may complete after H.

metric_definitions.total_effectiveness: E_total = sum_n e[agent_n,k_n], over all completed tasks.
metric_definitions.mean_effectiveness: E_bar = E_total/M; denominator is every received task.
metric_definitions.individual_effectiveness: Per-agent sum of assigned e values and mean per assigned task; these are model contributions, not measured competence.
metric_definitions.pending_work_at_H: At H, sum over unfinished assigned tasks of completion_time - max(service_start, H); this is the active task residual plus full service time of queued tasks, in service-time units. May be fractional.
metric_definitions.utilization_by_agent: For agent i, service time overlapping [0,H) divided by H; a proportion in [0,1].
metric_definitions.makespan: max_n completion_n - min_n arrival_n; elapsed time from first arrival to final completion.
metric_definitions.pending_task_count_at_H: Integer count of assigned tasks with completion_time > H; tasks completing exactly at H are complete. Includes the task in service and all queued tasks.
metric_definitions.completed_task_count_at_H: Integer count with completion_time <= H; received tasks are partitioned into completed and pending at H.
metric_definitions.fraction_completed_by_H: Tasks completed by H divided by all received tasks M.
metric_definitions.completed_effectiveness_total: Sum of fixed e[i,k] over tasks with completion_time <= H; a conditional modeled contribution, not an observed outcome.
metric_definitions.completed_effectiveness_mean: Completed effectiveness total divided by completed-task count; undefined when none complete by H.
metric_definitions.completed_response_mean_and_p95: Mean and nearest-rank P95 of completion_time-arrival_time among tasks completed by H only; separate from all-task response.

entities.name: Temporal workload effects in heterogeneous task allocation
entities.definition: Deterministic study comparing fixed, maximum-effectiveness and effectiveness/load-ratio assignment under temporally varying arrivals, recoverable per-agent service capacity, and declared effectiveness/demand/load profiles.
entities.scope: Six original controls, paired 96-cell sensitivity grid, five-structure focused controls, simultaneous-order probe, and exact small P2 response counterexample on constructed inputs. A separate restricted local-data replay applies the same model to SOCTRA alert-record timestamps as arrival proxies, with hypothetical organizations/effectiveness/service and no claim of human workload validity. A separately identified S0-S3 organization comparison adds minimum-pending-work, reuses the unchanged P1/P2 rules, and adds thresholded specialist-backup routing over four qualitative demand-pattern windows.
assumptions: One deterministic service duration per task class, shared by all agents in the baseline.
Every task is eventually completed; no deadlines or rejection.
Competence is not measured; e[i,k] is a constructed deterministic contribution.
Sensitivity profiles and traces are constructed; offered-load ratios are not observed utilization.
H0-H2 preserve per-class mean effectiveness at 0.6; H3 is a separate dominant-agent control and does not preserve those marginals.
Equal-time arrivals retain the supplied sequence order, which determines FCFS order when tasks join the same queue.
The restricted snapshot is not stored in Git; one alert row is treated only as a modeled arrival proxy, not a confirmed human task.
Project labels define opaque task classes for the experiment; project identity is not competence.
Timestamp meaning and timezone are not validated; exact stored order is used only under an explicit recorded-time assumption and simultaneous-order sensitivity.
Organization size, fixed effectiveness profiles, service durations, and offered-load levels are hypothetical and not calibrated to GMV-CERT staffing or analyst time.
entities.research_question: Under which deterministic arrival/load and fixed-effectiveness structures does routing by e[i,k]/(W_i+s_k) change response time and collective effectiveness relative to a fixed mapping and maximum-effectiveness routing?

entities.name: Six deterministic temporal allocation controls
entities.definition: Runs separated arrivals, balanced bursts, concentrated-class bursts, crossed specialization with block demand, homogeneous effectiveness, and agent dominance under matched policy inputs.
entities.scope: Small constructed fixtures with common demand, effectiveness, service times and resources across policies.
assumptions: All numeric durations and effectiveness profiles are dimensionless synthetic control values, not operational estimates.
No statistical inference is performed.

entities.name: Paired deterministic sensitivity grid for temporal allocation
entities.definition: Evaluates fixed P0 mappings, maximum-effectiveness P1 and effectiveness-to-current-workload P2 on the same 48-task traces across four deterministic effectiveness profiles, four demand profiles, two workforce sizes and three arrival horizons.
entities.scope: 96 H×D×N×horizon cells; no stochastic replication or statistical inference.
assumptions: Unit service duration for both task classes; all tasks eventually complete.

H0-H2 have per-class marginal mean 0.6; for N=4 the H1/H2 rows are interleaved to avoid confounding index-ordered fixed routing with profile order. H3 is a dominance control with different marginal means.
Offered load is total offered service divided by N times horizon; peak window ratio is separately reported and neither is observed utilization.
All effectiveness values, traces and durations are synthetic controls, not SOCTRA measurements.

entities.name: Workload-aware routing has scenario-dependent time-effectiveness tradeoffs
entities.definition: Across six constructed controls, P0 and P1 have the same assignments by scenario construction. P2 matches P1 in separated and balanced-burst cases; in concentrated, crossed-block and dominance cases P2 lowers mean response by 6.52–43.04% while mean effectiveness falls by 6.67–17.65%; for homogeneous effectiveness, P2 lowers response by 50% without changing mean effectiveness. Fixture-specific exact outputs only.
entities.scope: Exact deterministic runner output; no SOCTRA inference, sampling uncertainty or population claim.
assumptions: Every task completes and P1 independently maximizes fixed effectiveness per task.
Comparison percentages use P1 as denominator and are reported only for positive P1 metrics.

entities.name: Workload-aware allocation trades taskwise effectiveness for response in a subset of constructed regimes
entities.definition: In 96 deterministic cells, P2 response was faster than P1 in 54, equal in 42, and slower in none. Twenty-five faster cells had no effectiveness loss; 29 had lower effectiveness. P2 was not faster in 42 cells, with no effectiveness loss in those cells. P1 exceeded or matched each predeclared fixed baseline in all cells. Under the predeclared fixed duty-roster P0 contrast, five H3 cells had lower mean response under P0 than P2; these are fixed-mapping-specific, not a general ordering.
entities.scope: Exact descriptive outputs from the declared synthetic sensitivity grid; no statistical inference, SOC calibration or general policy ranking.
assumptions: All tasks complete; P1 selects a per-task effectiveness maximizer and therefore maximizes the deterministic effectiveness sum.
Relative comparisons are within the same cell and use identical tasks, matrix, service times, horizon and number of servers.

entities.name: Taskwise maximum effectiveness is an upper bound on total effectiveness
entities.definition: For fixed e[i,k], all agents eligible, unlimited queues and all tasks eventually completed, selecting an argmax_i e[i,k_n] independently for every task maximizes the sum of deterministic effectiveness contributions.
entities.scope: Effectiveness objective only; does not optimize waiting, response, makespan, utilization or throughput.
assumptions: Task contributions are unaffected by agent workload, queue position and completion time.
All tasks eventually complete and all agents are eligible for every task.

entities.name: Focused temporal allocation controls across five competence structures
entities.definition: Compares fixed, maximum-effectiveness and effectiveness-to-workload assignment for equivalent, crossed-specialist, moderately specialized, dominant-agent and partially polyvalent two-agent matrices under simultaneous balanced and class-concentrated bursts.
entities.scope: Ten deterministic constructed cells; N=2, 24 tasks, H=24, unit service by class; descriptive only.
assumptions: Effectiveness entries are fixed deterministic objective contributions, not success probabilities or empirical competence.
The fixed mapping is declared per structure before routing; no empirical SOC parameters are used.
All tasks are processed and queues drain; there are no deadlines, learning, cooperation or AI effects.

entities.name: Three-task counterexample to response optimality of load-ratio routing
entities.definition: Evaluates P1 and P2 on a three-task, two-agent, two-class deterministic sequence, first with equal service times and then with unequal class service times.
entities.scope: Exact small counterexample fixture; no statistical inference.
assumptions: Fixed effectiveness and positive deterministic class service times.
Same ordered arrivals, agents and inputs under both policies.

entities.name: Redistribution trades deterministic effectiveness for shorter responses in selected burst regimes
entities.definition: Across five constructed two-agent structures, P2 matched P1 on balanced bursts in equivalent, crossed, moderate-specialization and partially polyvalent cases; under class-concentrated bursts it shortened response by redistributing work, with structure-dependent effectiveness loss. In the dominance structure it also redistributed during balanced bursts.
entities.scope: Ten exact deterministic cells; descriptive scenario outcomes, not SOC evidence or a general policy ranking.
assumptions: Matrices, arrivals and unit service durations are synthetic and fixed.
No statistical inference is applied to the deterministic tasks.
entities.evidence_availability: regenerable from deterministic focused runner; no execution logs retained

entities.name: Effectiveness-to-workload routing is not generally response-optimal
entities.definition: A three-task exact counterexample gives P2 mean response 4/3 versus P1 7/6 with unit service times; with service times (1,2), P2 mean response is 5/3 versus P1 3/2. Both cases retain total effectiveness 0.8 and the same policy assignments.
entities.scope: Counterexample to a universal response-minimization guarantee for P2; does not establish general response optimality of P1.
assumptions: Two agents, two classes, fixed matrix ((0.2,0.2),(0.2,0.4)), arrivals ((0,0),(0.5,0),(0.5,1)).
The finite search for smaller examples covered only declared discrete effectiveness, arrival-time and service grids.
entities.evidence_availability: exact fixture reproducible by regression test; no raw logs needed

entities.name: Matched allocation replay on restricted timestamped alert-record demand
entities.definition: Replays anonymized project-class arrivals derived locally from the latest SOCTRA snapshot through the unchanged HLS-02 engine, comparing P0/P1/P2 under four hypothetical organizations and normalized service-load assumptions.
entities.scope: Exploratory deterministic replay of full recorded coverage, calendar year 2023, and a complete 12-month September 2024–August 2025 window; includes load, class-service-duration, class-to-organization alignment, and same-timestamp ordering sensitivities. A later scientific audit verified normalized-time, work-conservation, capacity and tie-break behavior. No analyst-hours or operational policy performance is estimated.
assumptions: Each unique alert record is a demand-arrival proxy; it is not asserted to be a human work episode.
The stored timestamp is used as relative event time; its timezone and operational meaning remain unverified.
Timestamps are mapped affinely to a unit horizon, preserving recorded order and relative gaps but not physical-time units.
Project labels are opaque task classes, not competence dimensions or named clients.
N=4, deterministic effectiveness contributions, service durations, and offered-load levels are hypothetical.

Offered load is total hypothetical service work divided by N times the unit horizon; it is neither realized utilization nor a per-agent queue load, and rho below one can coexist with transient or organizational backlog.
P0/P1/P2 use identical records, service parameters, organization matrix, and horizon within each paired condition; no raw data or row-level results are stored.

entities.name: Allocation policies trade response and effectiveness under SOCTRA alert-proxy replay
entities.definition: The matched local replay yields condition-dependent effects of fixed routing, taskwise maximum effectiveness, and effectiveness-to-workload routing under observed alert-record timing/project-class patterns. The output is conditional on proxy arrivals and hypothetical organization/service assumptions; it is not evidence about GMV-CERT analyst performance.
entities.scope: Deterministic exploratory simulations using restricted SOCTRA-derived demand records; no statistical inference across independent samples and no operational validation.
assumptions: Conclusions are conditional on the exact local snapshot, time interpretation, anonymous project-class ordering, chosen effectiveness matrices, hypothetical offered load, service profiles, and equal-time ordering rule.
The P1 taskwise effectiveness upper bound is a mathematical model property; observed policy trade-offs are scenario outputs.
Source rows and identifiers are unavailable in the repository, so exact output reproduction requires authorized access to the same snapshot.
entities.evidence_availability: Aggregate summary and adapter are tracked; the restricted CSV and row-level trace are not. Exact replay requires the authorized original snapshot.

entities.name: Online routing by minimum pending work
entities.definition: Assigns the current task to the agent minimizing W_i(t)=max(0,queue_tail_i-t), with lowest index breaking ties; ignores effectiveness.
entities.scope: Deterministic online rule in the organization-policy comparison.
assumptions: All agents can receive all task classes.
Only current observable queue-tail workload is used.
Queues are unbounded and no task is rejected.
entities.inputs: Current arrival time and all agent queue-tail completion times.

entities.name: Thresholded specialist routing with idle backup
entities.definition: Selects the maximum-effectiveness specialist (index tie-break). If its current W_i(t) exceeds theta*s_k, routes to the most effective other idle agent with e[i,k] at least a declared floor; otherwise uses the specialist. If no backup qualifies, uses the specialist.
entities.scope: Deterministic online heuristic; primary theta=1 and backup effectiveness floor=0.50; threshold sensitivity theta in {0.5,1,2}.
assumptions: Effectiveness is a hypothetical fixed contribution.
Service duration s_k is shared across agents and known.
Backup must be idle at arrival; queues are unbounded and no task is rejected.
entities.inputs: Current task class, fixed effectiveness matrix, observable queue workload, class service duration, threshold and effectiveness floor.

entities.name: Matched organization-policy comparison on demand-pattern windows
entities.definition: Compares minimum-work routing (S0), maximum-effectiveness routing (S1), effectiveness-load routing (S2), and thresholded specialist backup (S3) on four outcome-blind 28-day patterns extracted from a restricted SOCTRA alert-record snapshot.
entities.scope: Four hypothetical organization profiles, three normalized offered-load levels (0.50, 0.90, 1.20), shared fixed per-class service times and effectiveness within each paired cell. The alert stream supplies qualitative timing/class-pattern structure, not a human task rate.
assumptions: Each alert record is only a modeled arrival proxy.
Opaque project labels are task classes, not measured competencies or confirmed clients.
Team size, effectiveness, service durations and offered load are hypothetical.
Windows are selected using demand-only rules before policy evaluation.
All policies receive identical ordered arrivals, task classes, service times and horizon.

entities.name: Organization-policy trade-offs vary with competence structure and demand pattern
entities.definition: In 16 deterministic organization-by-window cells at rho=0.90, S0, S2 and S3 have lower all-task mean response than S1 in all cells. S1 gives the taskwise maximum effectiveness. S3 has equal or higher mean effectiveness than S0 but slower response in all 16 cells. These are outputs under constructed rosters and normalized alert-proxy patterns, not operational SOC effects.
entities.scope: Four 28-day demand-pattern windows x four four-agent hypothetical organizations, rho=0.90 primary and rho=0.50/1.20 sensitivity. No independent sampling unit or statistical inference.
assumptions: The restricted snapshot, timestamp interpretation, opaque class ordering, organization matrices, service scaling and tie-breaks condition the result.
Task completion by H is distinct from all-task response.
No claim is made about GMV-CERT performance, real clients, analyst competence, or a deployed policy.
entities.evidence_availability: The restricted CSV is not tracked. The runner, deterministic rules and aggregate findings are tracked; exact replay requires authorized access to the same snapshot.
